page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-16-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive and I/O-demanding enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 126.0 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation of approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains zero discrete GPU accelerators, orienting its resource allocation toward standard compute, elevated memory capacity, and substantial direct-attached storage.

The primary architectural highlight of the z4d-highmem-16-highlssd is its 7,516 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, supplied via two integrated drives. This direct-attached NVMe capacity provides high-throughput and low-latency physical disk access for applications that cannot tolerate network-attached storage latency. In terms of external networking, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring administrators to use private routing or assign network addresses separately.

From an efficiency perspective, integrating extensive NVMe SSD capacity directly with high memory density reduces the need for expensive external block storage arrays in transient or replicated architectures. This hardware profile is appropriate for high-performance transactional databases, distributed NoSQL databases, in-memory caches with persistent local disk logging, search index nodes, and large-scale data transformation pipelines.
